decision_log.rationale: User picked "both correlated" during prelaboration. This is the load-bearing choice that differentiates this tool from ccusage and similar — competitors report parent-session totals only and cannot answer "how much did this hat dispatch spend in the parent vs the subagents it spawned".

User explicitly named the skill /haiku:burn. Picked the colloquial term ("token burn") over the more literal alternatives. Sets vocabulary precedent for related future skills (e.g. /haiku:burn-compare).

options: Original 4 breakdowns only (intent / stage-hat / subagent / model)
Add by_tick as a 5th breakdown (one row per haiku_run_next call)
decision_log.choice: Add by_tick as a 5th breakdown (one row per haiku_run_next call)
decision_log.rationale: User requested per-tick visibility mid-elaboration. Per-tick attribution answers "which workflow tick burned the most" — load-bearing for engine optimization (which orchestrator action's prompt is most expensive, where to batch, where to trim).

input/output + user vs agent vs engine origin
decision_log.choice: input/output + user vs agent vs engine origin
decision_log.rationale: User explicitly added origin classification. The engine bucket (workflow contracts, MCP tool results, hook output, system reminders) is the single most actionable signal for engine-side optimization — it shows how much of every intent's spend is framework overhead vs real work.

options: JSON + Markdown + auto-upload to shareable URL
decision_log.rationale: User said "exportable so they can be sent to me and given back to the agent". JSON covers machine re-ingestion and diffing; Markdown covers human reading + agent paste-back via the Read tool. CSV deferred (derivable client-side from JSON; one of the discovery non-goals is "not a spreadsheet exporter"). Auto-upload deferred (introduces auth surface area the api-surface explicitly avoids). Surfaced for veto in unit-04 §Open questions.

decision_log.decision: Definition of a "tick" for by_tick attribution
options: One haiku_run_next call (parent-session work attributed to the action it returned)
One orchestrator phase transition (multiple haiku_run_next calls may map to one phase)
One day / one session (session-grain only, like ccusage)
decision_log.choice: One haiku_run_next call (parent-session work attributed to the action it returned)
decision_log.rationale: A tick already has a canonical identity in the engine: every action-log entry carries tick_counter (action-log.ts). Reusing that field means by_tick has no new on-disk state and no new derivation rule — the analyzer just reads tick_counter and groups. Phase-grain would smear the per-action signal the user wanted; session-grain is what every external tool already does.

decision_log.decision: Tool name for the new MCP entry point
decision_log.rationale: Tool name and skill name decouple intentionally: skill /haiku:burn is the colloquial agent surface; haiku_token_spend is the precise MCP descriptor that shows up in tools/list. Matches existing convention (skill /haiku:dashboard wraps tool haiku_dashboard semantically; the descriptive form wins for tool registry entries). Chosen by api-surface discovery agent and surfaced via this unit's body for veto.
